name: strkit-cst
about: strkit, with errors.py, the README and the changelog merged by tools/merge-cst (a syntax-tree merge driver) and __init__.py by union
common: Every function and error class you add is exported from `strkit/__init__.py` (one `from .MODULE import NAME` line per name, directly above `__all__ = [`, and one `    "NAME",` line per name directly above its closing `]`). Your error class goes in `strkit/errors.py` and subclasses `StrkitError`. Tests go in a test file of your own under `tests/`. In `README.md`, list each function under "Functions", one line each in the form `- strkit.NAME(ARGS): what it does`, replacing `- (none yet)` if it is still there, and add a section of your own (`## TOPIC`, after "Functions" and before "Errors") with a short example. In `CHANGELOG.md`, add one line under "Unreleased" for each function: `- Add strkit.NAME.`
tasks: Durations, in `strkit/durations.py`, with `DurationError`. `parse_duration(text) -> int` gives the seconds in a text such as `"1h30m"`, `"2d"`, `"45s"` or `"1h 30m 5s"`: each part a whole number and a unit, `d` (86400), `h` (3600), `m` (60) or `s` (1), letters in either case; parts in that order, each unit at most once, optional spaces between parts and around the whole. Anything else (empty text, a unit missing or unknown, a unit twice or out of order, a number with no digits) raises `DurationError`. `format_duration(seconds) -> str` is the reverse: the largest units first, parts that are zero left out, separated by one space (`5400` gives `"1h 30m"`, `90061` gives `"1d 1h 1m 1s"`), `"0s"` for 0; a negative number raises `DurationError`, and anything that is not an int (a bool is not) raises `TypeError`. The section is "Durations".

Roman numerals, in `strkit/roman.py`, with `RomanError`. `to_roman(n) -> str` gives the canonical numeral in capitals (`1994` gives `"MCMXCIV"`) for 1 to 3999; any other int raises `RomanError`, and anything that is not an int (a bool is not) raises `TypeError`. `from_roman(text) -> int` reads a numeral in either case, and only the canonical form: `"IIII"`, `"IC"`, `"VX"`, `"MMMM"`, the empty text and any other letter raise `RomanError`, so that `to_roman(from_roman(s)) == s.upper()` for every `s` it takes. The section is "Roman numerals".

Versions, in `strkit/versions.py`, with `VersionError`. `parse_version(text) -> Version`, where `Version` is a `typing.NamedTuple` with `major`, `minor`, `patch` (ints) and `pre` (a tuple, empty for a release) exported as well: `"1.2.3"` and `"1.2.3-alpha.1"` (`pre` is `("alpha", 1)`: identifiers of digits only are ints). Numbers with a leading zero (`"01.2.3"`, `"1.2.3-01"`), missing parts, empty identifiers, characters other than ASCII letters, digits and `-` in an identifier, and build metadata (`+...`) raise `VersionError`. `compare_versions(a, b) -> int` is -1, 0 or 1 by Semantic Versioning 2.0 precedence for two texts: major, minor, patch numerically; a version with `pre` is below the same one without; `pre` compared identifier by identifier, ints numerically and below texts, texts in ASCII order, and a shorter `pre` below a longer one it begins. `bump(text, part) -> str` with `part` one of `"major"`, `"minor"`, `"patch"`: that number up by one, those after it 0, `pre` dropped (`bump("1.2.3-rc.1", "minor")` is `"1.3.0"`); any other part raises `VersionError`. The section is "Versions".

Templates, in `strkit/templates.py`, with `TemplateError`. `render(template, context) -> str` replaces each `{NAME}` by `str()` of `context[NAME]`; a name may be dotted (`{user.name}`), each step a key where the value is a dict and an attribute otherwise. A name may be followed by filters, applied left to right: `{name|upper}`, `|lower`, `|title`, `|strip`, and `|default:TEXT`, which gives TEXT where the name is missing or its value is `None` (TEXT runs to the next `|` or to the `}`, and may be empty). `{{` and `}}` are a literal `{` and `}`. A name that is missing with no `default`, an unknown filter, an empty name, a `{` with no `}` and a `}` on its own raise `TemplateError`. The section is "Templates".
